verses.1:1: Now Solomon the son of David strengthened himself in his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and exalted him exceedingly.
verses.1:2: And Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel, the heads of the fathers' houses.
verses.1:3: Then Solomon, and all the assembly with him, went to the high place that was at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God was there, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness.
verses.1:4: However, David had brought up the ark of God from Kiriath Jearim to the place David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
verses.1:5: Moreover, the bronze altar that Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made was there before the tabernacle of the LORD, and Solomon and the assembly sought Him.
verses.1:6: And Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD, which belonged to the tent of meeting, and offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it.
verses.1:7: On that night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I shall give you."
verses.1:8: And Solomon said to God, "You have shown great lovingkindness to David my father, and have made me king in his place.
verses.1:9: Now, O LORD God, let Your word to David my father be confirmed, for You have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
verses.1:10: Now grant me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this great people of Yours?"
verses.1:11: Then God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked for riches, wealth, or honor, nor the life of those who hate you, nor have you even asked for long life, but have asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself, that you may judge My people over whom I have made you king,
verses.1:12: wisdom and knowledge are granted to you; and I will give you riches and wealth and honor, such as none of the kings before you have had, nor shall any after you have the like."
verses.1:13: So Solomon came to Jerusalem from before the tent of meeting at the high place that was in Gibeon, and he reigned over Israel.
verses.1:14: And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen; he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.1:15: Also the king made silver and gold in Jerusalem as common as stones, and he made cedars as abundant as the sycamores that are in the lowland.
verses.1:16: And Solomon's import of horses was from Egypt and from Kue; the king's merchants acquired them from Kue at a price.
verses.1:17: They brought up and imported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty; and thus by their hand they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
verses.1:18: Now Solomon purposed to build a house for the name of the LORD, and a house for his kingdom.
verses.2:1: And Solomon numbered seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand men to quarry in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.
verses.2:2: Then Solomon sent to Huram king of Tyre, saying, "As you dealt with David my father and sent him cedars to build himself a house to dwell in,
verses.2:3: behold, I am building a house for the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to Him, to burn fragrant incense before Him, for the continual showbread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, on the New Moons, and on the appointed feasts of the LORD our God; this is appointed forever for Israel.
verses.2:4: And the house which I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all the gods.
verses.2:5: But who has strength to build Him a house, since heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him? And who am I that I should build Him a house, except to burn incense before Him?
verses.2:6: Therefore now send me a skilled man to work in gold and silver, in bronze and iron, in purple and crimson and blue, and who knows how to make engravings, to work with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.
verses.2:7: Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut the timber of Lebanon; and behold, my servants will be with your servants,
verses.2:8: to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house which I am building will be great and wonderful.
verses.2:9: And behold, I will give to your servants, the woodsmen who cut the timber, twenty thousand kors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand kors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."
verses.2:10: Then Huram king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves His people, He has made you king over them."
verses.2:11: Huram also said, "Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, for He has given King David a wise son, endowed with prudence and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a house for his kingdom!
verses.2:12: And now I have sent a skilled man, endowed with understanding, Huram-Abi,
verses.2:13: the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre, skilled to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, purple and blue, fine linen and crimson, and to make any engraving and devise any design that may be assigned to him, together with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.
verses.2:14: Now therefore, the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine of which my lord has spoken, let him send to his servants.
verses.2:15: And we will cut whatever timber you need from Lebanon, and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Joppa; and you shall carry it up to Jerusalem."
verses.2:16: Then Solomon numbered all the men who were sojourners in the land of Israel, after the census by which David his father had numbered them; and there were found one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
verses.2:17: And he appointed seventy thousand of them to bear burdens, eighty thousand to quarry in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred as overseers to set the people to work.
verses.3:1: Now Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where He had appeared to David his father, which he prepared at the place of David, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.3:2: And he began to build on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
verses.3:3: Now these are the foundation measurements which Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length in cubits according to the former measure was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
verses.3:4: And the vestibule in front of the house was twenty cubits in length across the width of the house, and its height was one hundred and twenty cubits; and he overlaid it on the inside with pure gold.
verses.3:5: And the main hall he paneled with cypress wood, overlaid it with fine gold, and set palm trees and chains upon it.
verses.3:6: He also adorned the house with precious stones for beauty, and the gold was gold of Parvaim.
verses.3:7: And he overlaid the house—the beams, the thresholds, its walls, and its doors—with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
verses.3:8: And he made the Most Holy Place: its length across the width of the house was twenty cubits, and its width was twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
verses.3:9: And the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold; he also overlaid the upper chambers with gold.
verses.3:10: In the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculpted work, and they overlaid them with gold.
verses.3:11: The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits in total length: one wing of the first was five cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing was five cubits, touching the wing of the other cherub;
verses.3:12: and one wing of the other cherub was five cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing was five cubits, joined to the wing of the first cherub.
verses.3:13: The wings of these cherubim spanned twenty cubits; they stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.
verses.3:14: And he made the veil of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and worked cherubim upon it.
verses.3:15: Also he made in front of the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high, and the capital on the top of each was five cubits.
verses.3:16: And he made chains in the inner sanctuary and put them on the tops of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.
verses.3:17: And he set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and the other on the left; he called the name of the one on the right Jachin, and the name of the one on the left Boaz.
verses.4:1: And he made an altar of bronze: twenty cubits was its length, twenty cubits its width, and ten cubits its height.
verses.4:2: He also made the molten Sea, ten cubits from one brim to the other, round all around; its height was five cubits, and a line of thirty cubits encompassed it all around.
verses.4:3: And beneath it was the likeness of oxen encircling it all around, ten to a cubit, surrounding the Sea on every side; the oxen were in two rows, cast when it was cast.
verses.4:4: It stood upon twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east; the Sea was set upon them above, and all their hindquarters pointed inward.
verses.4:5: Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom; it held three thousand baths.
verses.4:6: He also made ten lavers, and placed five on the right side and five on the left, to wash in them; what pertained to the burnt offering they would rinse in them, while the Sea was for the priests to wash in.
verses.4:7: And he made ten lampstands of gold according to their prescribed form, and set them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left.
verses.4:8: He also made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left; and he made one hundred bowls of gold.
verses.4:9: Furthermore he made the court of the priests, and the great court, and doors for the court; and their doors he overlaid with bronze.
verses.4:10: And he set the Sea on the right side, toward the east, facing the south.
verses.4:11: Then Huram made the pots, the shovels, and the bowls. Thus Huram finished doing the work that he performed for King Solomon in the house of God:
verses.4:12: the two pillars, the two bowls and capitals upon the top of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars;
verses.4:13: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks—two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the pillars.
verses.4:14: He also made the stands, and he made the lavers upon the stands,
verses.4:15: the one Sea, and the twelve oxen beneath it.
verses.4:16: Also the pots, the shovels, the forks, and all their vessels Huram his master craftsman made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD, of burnished bronze.
verses.4:17: In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredathah.
verses.4:18: And Solomon made all these vessels in exceedingly great abundance, for the weight of the bronze was not ascertained.
verses.4:19: So Solomon made all the furnishings that were in the house of God: the altar of gold, and the tables upon which the showbread was set;
verses.4:20: and the lampstands with their lamps of pure gold, to burn according to the ordinance before the inner sanctuary;
verses.4:21: and the blossoms, the lamps, and the tongs of gold—the purest of gold;
verses.4:22: and the trimmers, the bowls, the ladles, and the firepans of pure gold; and as for the entrance of the house, its inner doors for the Most Holy Place and the doors of the house for the temple were of gold.
verses.5:1: Thus all the work that Solomon performed for the house of the LORD was completed. And Solomon brought in the dedicated things of his father David; the silver, the gold, and all the vessels he placed in the treasuries of the house of God.
verses.5:2: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the chief fathers of the children of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David, which is Zion.
verses.5:3: So all the men of Israel assembled before the king at the feast, which was in the seventh month.
verses.5:4: And all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites took up the ark.
verses.5:5: And they brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; the Levitical priests brought them up.
verses.5:6: Now King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who had gathered with him before the ark were sacrificing sheep and oxen that could neither be counted nor numbered for multitude.
verses.5:7: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, into the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.5:8: For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim overshadowed the ark and its poles from above.
verses.5:9: And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles were visible from the ark before the inner sanctuary, yet they could not be seen from outside; and it remains there to this day.
verses.5:10: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the children of Israel when they came out of Egypt.
verses.5:11: Now it came to pass when the priests came out of the Holy Place—for all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves, without keeping to their divisions—
verses.5:12: and the Levitical singers, all of them, of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, together with their sons and their brethren, clothed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, stood east of the altar, and with them one hundred and twenty priests blowing trumpets—
verses.5:13: it came to pass, when the trumpeters and the singers were as one, to make one sound heard in praising and giving thanks to the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying, "For He is good, for His lovingkindness endures forever," that the house, even the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud,
verses.5:14: so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
verses.6:1: Then Solomon spoke: "The LORD has said He would dwell in the thick darkness.
verses.6:2: And I have built an exalted house for You, a settled place for Your dwelling forever."
verses.6:3: Then the king turned his face around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel was standing.
verses.6:4: And he said: "Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, who spoke with His mouth to my father David, and with His hands has fulfilled it, saying,
verses.6:5: 'Since the day that I brought My people out from the land of Egypt, I have not chosen any city from all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, that My name might be there; nor did I choose any man to be a ruler over My people Israel.
verses.6:6: Yet I have chosen Jerusalem, that My name might be there; and I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.'
verses.6:7: Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of the LORD God of Israel.
verses.6:8: But the LORD said to my father David, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for My name, you did well that it was in your heart.
verses.6:9: Nevertheless, you shall not build the house; rather your son who shall come forth from your own loins, he shall build the house for My name.'
verses.6:10: So the LORD has established His word which He spoke, and I have risen in the place of my father David and sit upon the throne of Israel, just as the LORD spoke; and I have built the house for the name of the LORD God of Israel.
verses.6:11: And there I have set the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that He made with the children of Israel."
verses.6:12: Then he stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of the whole assembly of Israel, and spread forth his hands.
verses.6:13: For Solomon had made a bronze platform, five cubits in its length, five cubits in its width, and three cubits in its height, and had placed it in the midst of the court; and he stood upon it, and knelt down upon his knees in the presence of the whole assembly of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward heaven.
verses.6:14: And he said: "O LORD God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven or on earth, who keeps the covenant and lovingkindness with Your servants who walk before You with all their heart.
verses.6:15: You have kept with Your servant David my father what You promised him; indeed, You spoke with Your mouth and have fulfilled it with Your hand, as it is this day.
verses.6:16: Therefore now, O LORD God of Israel, keep with Your servant David my father what You spoke to him, saying, 'You shall not fail to have a man before Me sitting upon the throne of Israel, if only your sons take heed to their way, to walk in My law as you have walked before Me.'
verses.6:17: Now then, O LORD God of Israel, let Your word be confirmed, which You have spoken to Your servant David.
verses.6:18: But will God indeed dwell with mankind upon the earth? Behold, heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain You—how much less this house which I have built!
verses.6:19: Yet turn toward the prayer of Your servant and his supplication, O LORD my God, to listen to the cry and the prayer which Your servant is praying before You:
verses.6:20: that Your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward the place where You have said You would put Your name, to hear the prayer which Your servant prays toward this place.
verses.6:21: And hear the supplications of Your servant and of Your people Israel, when they pray toward this place; hear from the place of Your dwelling, from heaven, and when You hear, forgive.
verses.6:22: If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath is laid upon him to make him swear, and he comes and swears an oath before Your altar in this house,
verses.6:23: then hear from heaven, and act, and judge Your servants, requiting the wicked by bringing his way upon his own head, and justifying the righteous by giving to him according to his righteousness.
verses.6:24: And if Your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return and confess Your name, and pray and make supplication before You in this house,
verses.6:25: then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land which You gave to them and to their fathers.
verses.6:26: When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against You, if they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and turn from their sin when You afflict them,
verses.6:27: then hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel, for You teach them the good way in which they should walk; and send rain upon Your land which You have given to Your people as an inheritance.
verses.6:28: When there is famine in the land, when there is pestilence, blight or mildew, locust or caterpillar, when their enemies besiege them in the land of their gates, whatever plague or whatever sickness there is,
verses.6:29: whatever prayer, whatever supplication is made by any man, or by all Your people Israel, when each one knows his own affliction and his own grief, and spreads forth his hands toward this house,
verses.6:30: then hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and forgive, and render to every man according to all his ways, whose heart You know—for You, You alone, know the hearts of the sons of men—
verses.6:31: that they may fear You, to walk in Your ways all the days that they live upon the face of the land which You gave to our fathers.
verses.6:32: Moreover, concerning the foreigner, who is not of Your people Israel, yet comes from a distant land for the sake of Your great name and Your mighty hand and Your outstretched arm, when they come and pray toward this house,
verses.6:33: then hear from heaven, from Your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to You, in order that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and that they may know that this house which I have built is called by Your name.
verses.6:34: When Your people go out to battle against their enemies, by whatever way You shall send them, and they pray to You toward this city which You have chosen and the house which I have built for Your name,
verses.6:35: then hear from heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.
verses.6:36: When they sin against You—for there is no man who does not sin—and You become angry with them and deliver them before an enemy, so that their captors carry them away captive to a land far off or near,
verses.6:37: yet if they take it to heart in the land where they have been carried captive, and repent and make supplication to You in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned, we have committed iniquity, and we have acted wickedly,'
verses.6:38: and if they return to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity, where they have carried them captive, and pray toward their land which You gave to their fathers, and the city which You have chosen, and toward the house which I have built for Your name,
verses.6:39: then hear from heaven, from Your dwelling place, their prayer and their supplications, and maintain their cause, and forgive Your people who have sinned against You.
verses.6:40: Now, my God, I pray, let Your eyes be open and let Your ears be attentive to the prayer made in this place.
verses.6:41: Now therefore, arise, O LORD God, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength. Let Your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and let Your godly ones rejoice in goodness.
verses.6:42: O LORD God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed; remember the mercies of Your servant David."
verses.7:1: Now when Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the house.
verses.7:2: And the priests could not enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD.
verses.7:3: When all the children of Israel saw how the fire came down, and the glory of the LORD upon the house, they bowed their faces to the ground upon the pavement, and worshiped, giving thanks to the LORD: "For He is good, for His lovingkindness endures forever."
verses.7:4: Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
verses.7:5: King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. Thus the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.
verses.7:6: And the priests stood at their posts of duty, and the Levites with the musical instruments of the LORD, which King David had made to give thanks to the LORD—"For His lovingkindness endures forever"—whenever David offered praise through their hands; and the priests sounded trumpets opposite them, while all Israel stood.
verses.7:7: Furthermore, Solomon consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD; for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar which Solomon had made was not able to contain the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat.
verses.7:8: At that same time Solomon kept the feast seven days, and all Israel with him, an exceedingly great assembly from the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of Egypt.
verses.7:9: And on the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for they observed the dedication of the altar seven days, and the feast seven days.
verses.7:10: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for the goodness that the LORD had shown to David, to Solomon, and to His people Israel.
verses.7:11: Thus Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the house of the king; and Solomon prosperously accomplished all that came into his heart to make in the house of the LORD and in his own house.
verses.7:12: Then the LORD appeared to Solomon by night, and said to him: "I have heard your prayer, and have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.
verses.7:13: When I shut up the heavens and there is no rain, or command the locust to devour the land, or send pestilence among My people,
verses.7:14: if My people, upon whom My name is called, humble themselves, and pray and seek My countenance, and turn from their evil ways, then I Myself will hear from heaven, and I will forgive their sin and heal their land.
verses.7:15: Now My eyes shall be open and My ears attentive to the prayer made in this place.
verses.7:16: For now I have chosen and consecrated this house, that My name may be there forever; and My eyes and My heart shall be there continually.
verses.7:17: As for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and keep My statutes and My judgments,
verses.7:18: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom, just as I covenanted with your father David, saying, 'You shall not fail to have a man ruling in Israel.'
verses.7:19: But if you turn away and forsake My statutes and My commandments which I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,
verses.7:20: then I will uproot them from My land which I have given them; and this house which I have consecrated for My name I will cast out of My sight, and will make it a proverb and a byword among all peoples.
verses.7:21: And as for this house, which was so exalted, everyone who passes by it will be astonished and say, 'Why has the LORD done thus to this land and to this house?'
verses.7:22: Then they will answer, 'Because they forsook the LORD God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold of other gods, and bowed down to them and served them; therefore He has brought all this calamity upon them.'"
verses.8:1: Now it came to pass at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own house,
verses.8:2: that Solomon rebuilt the cities which Huram had given to Solomon, and caused the children of Israel to dwell there.
verses.8:3: And Solomon went to Hamath Zobah and prevailed against it.
verses.8:4: He also built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the storage cities which he built in Hamath.
verses.8:5: He built Upper Beth Horon and Lower Beth Horon, fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars;
verses.8:6: also Baalath, and all the storage cities that belonged to Solomon, and all the chariot cities and the cities of the horsemen, and every desire of Solomon which he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
verses.8:7: As for all the people who remained of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not of Israel,
verses.8:8: of their children who were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel had not destroyed, Solomon levied them for forced labor to this day.
verses.8:9: But Solomon did not appoint any of the children of Israel as servants for his work; for they were men of war, commanders of his officers, and commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.
verses.8:10: And these were the chief officers of King Solomon, two hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people.
verses.8:11: Now Solomon brought the daughter of Pharaoh up from the City of David to the house that he had built for her; for he said, "My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because the places to which the ark of the LORD has come are holy."
verses.8:12: Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD which he had built before the vestibule,
verses.8:13: even according to the daily rate, offering according to the commandment of Moses for the Sabbaths, for the New Moons, and for the appointed feasts three times a year: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, at the Feast of Weeks, and at the Feast of Tabernacles.
verses.8:14: And he appointed, according to the ordinance of David his father, the divisions of the priests to their service, and the Levites to their charges, to praise and to minister before the priests as the duty of every day required, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at every gate; for so was the commandment of David the man of God.
verses.8:15: And they did not turn aside from the commandment of the king concerning the priests and the Levites in any matter, or concerning the treasuries.
verses.8:16: Thus all the work of Solomon was established, up to the day the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid and until it was completed; so the house of the LORD was finished.
verses.8:17: Then Solomon went to Ezion Geber and to Eloth on the shore of the sea, in the land of Edom.
verses.8:18: And Huram sent him ships by the hand of his servants, and servants who knew the sea; and they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and took from there four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.
verses.9:1: Now when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with hard questions, with a very great retinue, and camels bearing spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones; and when she came to Solomon, she spoke with him concerning all that was in her heart.
verses.9:2: And Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hidden from Solomon which he did not explain to her.
verses.9:3: And when the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he had built,
verses.9:4: the food on his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his ministers and their apparel, his cupbearers and their apparel, and his ascent by which he went up to the house of the LORD, there was no more spirit in her.
verses.9:5: Then she said to the king, "The report was true which I heard in my own land concerning your words and your wisdom.
verses.9:6: Yet I did not believe their words until I came and my own eyes saw it; and behold, half of the greatness of your wisdom was not told to me. You have surpassed the report that I heard.
verses.9:7: Happy are your men, and happy are these your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
verses.9:8: Blessed be the LORD your God, who delighted in you, setting you on His throne to be king for the LORD your God! Because your God loved Israel, to establish them forever, therefore He made you king over them, to execute judgment and righteousness."
verses.9:9: And she gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, spices in very great abundance, and precious stones; and there were never any spices like those which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.9:10: Moreover, the servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum wood and precious stones.
verses.9:11: And from the algum wood the king made terraces for the house of the LORD and for the house of the king, as well as harps and stringed instruments for the singers; and none like them had ever been seen before in the land of Judah.
verses.9:12: And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked, besides what she had brought to the king. So she turned and departed to her own land, she and her servants.
verses.9:13: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
verses.9:14: besides what the traveling merchants and traders brought. And all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land brought gold and silver to Solomon.
verses.9:15: And King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of hammered gold went into each large shield.
verses.9:16: He also made three hundred smaller shields of hammered gold; three hundred shekels of gold went into each shield. And the king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
verses.9:17: Moreover, the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold.
verses.9:18: There were six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold fastened to the throne, armrests on either side of the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
verses.9:19: And twelve lions stood there on the six steps, one on each side; nothing like it had ever been made for any kingdom.
verses.9:20: All the drinking vessels of King Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; silver was not accounted as anything in the days of Solomon.
verses.9:21: For the ships of the king went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram. Once every three years the ships of Tarshish would come, bringing gold and silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
verses.9:22: Thus King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
verses.9:23: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
verses.9:24: Each man brought his tribute: vessels of silver and vessels of gold, garments, armor, spices, horses, and mules, a set rate year by year.
verses.9:25: And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.9:26: And he ruled over all the kings from the River even to the land of the Philistines, and as far as the border of Egypt.
verses.9:27: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedar trees as abundant as the sycamores which are in the lowland.
verses.9:28: And they brought horses to Solomon from Egypt and from all the lands.
verses.9:29: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat?
verses.9:30: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
verses.9:31: Then Solomon slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David his father. And Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:1: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
verses.10:2: Now it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard it—for he was in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of King Solomon—that Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
verses.10:3: Then they sent and called him. So Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.10:4: "Your father made our yoke harsh; now therefore, lighten the harsh service of your father and his heavy yoke which he laid upon us, and we will serve you."
verses.10:5: And he said to them, "Return to me after three days." So the people departed.
verses.10:6: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he still lived, saying, "How do you counsel me to return an answer to this people?"
verses.10:7: And they spoke to him, saying, "If you are kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever."
verses.10:8: But he forsook the counsel of the elders which they had given him, and consulted with the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
verses.10:9: And he said to them, "What do you advise that we should answer this people who have spoken to me, saying, 'Lighten the yoke which your father laid upon us'?"
verses.10:10: And the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, "Thus you shall speak to the people who have spoken to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you make it lighter for us'—thus you shall say to them: 'My little finger is thicker than the loins of my father!
verses.10:11: And now, whereas my father loaded you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions!'"
verses.10:12: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
verses.10:13: Then the king answered them harshly; and King Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the elders,
verses.10:14: and spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, "I will make your yoke heavy, and I will add to it; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions!"
verses.10:15: So the king did not listen to the people; for the turn of events was from God, that the LORD might fulfill His word, which He had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.10:16: Now as for all Israel, because the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king, saying, "What portion do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to your tents, O Israel! Now see to your own house, O David!" So all Israel departed to their tents.
verses.10:17: But as for the children of Israel who dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
verses.10:18: Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was over the forced labor; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. Therefore King Rehoboam made haste to mount the chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
verses.10:19: So Israel rebelled against the house of David to this day.
verses.11:1: Now Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, and he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand chosen men who were warriors, to fight against Israel, that he might restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
verses.11:2: Then the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
verses.11:3: "Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying,
verses.11:4: 'Thus says the LORD: You shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren. Return, every man to his house, for this thing has come from Me.'" So they listened to the words of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam.
verses.11:5: And Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem, and he built cities for defense in Judah.
verses.11:6: He built Bethlehem, Etam, and Tekoa,
verses.11:10: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, which are in Judah and in Benjamin, fortified cities.
verses.11:11: And he strengthened the fortresses, and placed commanders in them, with stores of food, oil, and wine.
verses.11:12: In every single city he put large shields and spears, and he made them exceedingly strong. Thus Judah and Benjamin belonged to him.
verses.11:13: Moreover, the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel presented themselves to him from all their territories.
verses.11:14: For the Levites left their pasturelands and their possessions and came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from serving as priests to the LORD.
verses.11:15: And he appointed for himself priests for the high places, for the goat idols, and for the calves that he had made.
verses.11:16: And after them, out of all the tribes of Israel, those who set their heart to seek the LORD God of Israel came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD God of their fathers.
verses.11:17: So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong for three years, because they walked in the way of David and Solomon for three years.
verses.11:18: Now Rehoboam took for himself as wife Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, and of Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse.
verses.11:19: And she bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
verses.11:20: After her he took Maacah the daughter of Absalom; and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
verses.11:21: Now Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and his concubines; for he took eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
verses.11:22: And Rehoboam appointed Abijah the son of Maacah as chief, to be leader among his brethren, for he intended to make him king.
verses.11:23: And he dealt wisely, and dispersed some of all his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to every fortified city; he gave them provisions in abundance, and sought many wives for them.
verses.12:1: Now it came to pass, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and he had become strong, that he forsook the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.
verses.12:2: And it happened in the fifth year of King Rehoboam that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had acted unfaithfully against the LORD,
verses.12:3: with one thousand two hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen, and people without number who came with him out of Egypt—the Lubim, the Sukkiim, and the Cushites.
verses.12:4: And he captured the fortified cities that belonged to Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.
verses.12:5: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah, who had gathered together at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, "Thus says the LORD: 'You have forsaken Me, and I also have forsaken you into the hand of Shishak.'"
verses.12:6: So the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, "The LORD is righteous."
verses.12:7: Now when the LORD saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, saying, "They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them a measure of deliverance, and My wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
verses.12:8: Nevertheless they shall be his servants, so that they may know My service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands."
verses.12:9: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house; he took everything. He also took away the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
verses.12:10: Then King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place, and committed them to the hands of the captains of the guard who kept the doorway of the king's house.
verses.12:11: And it was so, whenever the king entered the house of the LORD, that the guards would come and carry them, and then bring them back into the guardroom.
verses.12:12: When he humbled himself, the wrath of the LORD turned away from him, so as not to destroy him completely; and moreover, there were good things in Judah.
verses.12:13: Thus King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned. Now Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
verses.12:14: And he did evil, because he did not prepare his heart to seek the LORD.
verses.12:15: Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
verses.12:16: So Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the City of David. Then Abijah his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:1: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
verses.13:2: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
verses.13:3: Abijah entered into battle with an army of valiant warriors, four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam drew up in battle array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty men of valor.
verses.13:4: Then Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel:
verses.13:5: Should you not know that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, to him and his sons, by a covenant of salt?
verses.13:6: Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up and rebelled against his lord.
verses.13:7: Then worthless men, sons of Belial, gathered to him and strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and fainthearted and could not withstand them.
verses.13:8: And now you think to withstand the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hand of the sons of David; and you are a great multitude, and with you are the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.
verses.13:9: Have you not cast out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made for yourselves priests like the peoples of other lands, so that whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams may become a priest of what are not gods?
verses.13:10: But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken Him; and the priests who minister to the LORD are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites attend to their work.
verses.13:11: And they burn to the LORD every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and fragrant incense; the showbread is set upon the pure table, and the golden lampstand with its lamps is lit every evening; for we keep the charge of the LORD our God, but you have forsaken Him.
verses.13:12: And behold, God Himself is with us at our head, and His priests with the trumpets of alarm to sound the blast against you. O children of Israel, do not fight against the LORD God of your fathers, for you shall not succeed."
verses.13:13: But Jeroboam had sent an ambush around to come up from behind them; so his troops were in front of Judah, and the ambush was behind them.
verses.13:14: When Judah looked back, behold, the battle was before and behind them; and they cried out to the LORD, while the priests sounded the trumpets.
verses.13:15: Then the men of Judah raised a battle shout; and as the men of Judah shouted, God struck down Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
verses.13:16: And the children of Israel fled before Judah, and God delivered them into their hand.
verses.13:17: Then Abijah and his people struck them with a great slaughter; so five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell slain.
verses.13:18: Thus the children of Israel were subdued at that time; and the children of Judah prevailed, because they relied on the LORD God of their fathers.
verses.13:19: And Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured cities from him: Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephrain with its villages.
verses.13:20: And Jeroboam did not recover strength again in the days of Abijah; and the LORD struck him, and he died.
verses.13:21: But Abijah grew mighty, and took for himself fourteen wives, and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
verses.13:22: Now the rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways, and his sayings are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
verses.13:23: So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David. Then Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land was quiet for ten years.
verses.14:1: And Asa did what was good and upright in the eyes of the LORD his God.
verses.14:2: He removed the foreign altars and the high places, shattered the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles.
verses.14:3: He also commanded Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to observe the law and the commandment.
verses.14:4: Moreover he removed from all the cities of Judah the high places and the incense altars, and the kingdom was quiet before him.
verses.14:5: He built fortified cities in Judah, for the land was at rest; he had no war in those years, because the LORD had granted him rest.
verses.14:6: Therefore he said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, gates and bars. The land is still before us, because we have sought the LORD our God; we have sought Him, and He has granted us rest on every side." So they built and prospered.
verses.14:7: And Asa had an army of three hundred thousand from Judah who bore large shields and spears, and two hundred and eighty thousand from Benjamin who carried shields and drew bows; all of these were mighty men of valor.
verses.14:8: Then Zerah the Cushite marched out against them with an army of one million men and three hundred chariots, and he came as far as Mareshah.
verses.14:9: So Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up in battle array in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
verses.14:10: And Asa cried out to the LORD his God and said, "O LORD, it is nothing for You to help, whether the mighty or those who have no strength; help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on You, and in Your name we have come against this multitude. O LORD, You are our God; let no mortal man prevail against You."
verses.14:11: So the LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.
verses.14:12: Asa and the people who were with him pursued them as far as Gerar, and so many of the Cushites fell that no life remained among them, for they were broken before the LORD and before His host; and they carried away exceedingly much plunder.
verses.14:13: They also struck all the cities around Gerar, for the dread of the LORD had fallen upon them; and they plundered all the cities, because great spoil was in them.
verses.14:14: They struck the tents of livestock as well, captured sheep in great abundance and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.15:1: Now the Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded.
verses.15:2: And he went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: the LORD is with you while you are with Him. If you seek Him, He will let Himself be found by you; yet if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.
verses.15:3: For many days Israel was without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without the law;
verses.15:4: but in their distress they turned back to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought Him, and He was found by them.
verses.15:5: In those times there was no peace for the one going out or the one coming in, for great tumults afflicted all the inhabitants of the lands.
verses.15:6: Nation was crushed by nation and city by city, for God threw them into turmoil with every kind of distress.
verses.15:7: As for you, therefore, be strong, and do not let your hands grow weak, for your work shall have its reward."
verses.15:8: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage and put away the detestable idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities that he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. He also renewed the altar of the LORD that stood before the vestibule of the LORD.
verses.15:9: Then he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, along with those who sojourned with them from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon; for great numbers from Israel had defected to him when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
verses.15:10: So they assembled at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.15:11: And on that day they sacrificed to the LORD from the spoil they had brought seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
verses.15:12: Then they entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and with all their soul;
verses.15:13: and whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
verses.15:14: They swore an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets, and with horns.
verses.15:15: And all Judah rejoiced concerning the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and sought Him with all their desire, and He was found by them; and the LORD granted them rest on every side.
verses.15:16: King Asa also removed his mother Maachah from the office of queen mother, because she had made a repulsive image for Asherah; and Asa cut down her repulsive image, crushed it, and burned it at the Brook Kidron.
verses.15:17: Yet the high places were not removed from Israel; nevertheless, Asa's heart remained wholly devoted all his days.
verses.15:18: He also brought into the house of God the dedicated things of his father and his own dedicated things—silver and gold and vessels.
verses.15:19: And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.16:1: In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and built Ramah, so that he might allow no one to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.16:2: Then Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house, and sent them to Ben-Hadad king of Aram, who dwelt in Damascus, saying,
verses.16:3: "Let there be a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you silver and gold; come, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he may withdraw from me."
verses.16:4: So Ben-Hadad heeded King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they struck Ijon, Dan, Abel Maim, and all the storehouses of the cities of Naphtali.
verses.16:5: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard of it, that he stopped building Ramah and ceased his work.
verses.16:6: Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried away the stones and timber of Ramah with which Baasha had been building, and with them he built Geba and Mizpah.
verses.16:7: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you relied on the king of Aram, and did not rely on the LORD your God, therefore the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
verses.16:8: Were not the Cushites and the Lubim a massive host with exceedingly many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the LORD, He delivered them into your hand.
verses.16:9: For the eyes of the LORD roam across all the earth, to prove Himself strong for those whose heart is undivided toward Him. You have acted foolishly in this; indeed, from this time forward you shall have wars."
verses.16:10: Then Asa grew angry with the seer and put him in the stocks, for he was in a rage against him over this; and Asa oppressed some of the people at that same time.
verses.16:11: Now behold, the acts of Asa, first and last, are indeed written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.16:12: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his illness grew exceedingly severe; yet even in his illness he did not seek the LORD, but only the physicians.
verses.16:13: So Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the forty-first year of his reign.
verses.16:14: They buried him in his own tomb, which he had hewn out for himself in the City of David; and they laid him on a bier filled with spices and various perfumes blended by the perfumer's craft. And they made an exceedingly great fire in his honor.
verses.17:1: Then Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and he strengthened himself against Israel.
verses.17:2: And he placed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah, and set garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had captured.
verses.17:3: Now the LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David and did not seek the Baals.
verses.17:4: Rather, he sought the God of his father and walked in His commandments, and not according to the deeds of Israel.
verses.17:5: Therefore the LORD established the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah gave tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had wealth and honor in abundance.
verses.17:6: And his heart was emboldened in the ways of the LORD; moreover, he removed the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah.
verses.17:7: Also in the third year of his reign he sent his officials—Ben-Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah—to teach in the cities of Judah.
verses.17:8: And with them were the Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah, the Levites; and with them Elishama and Jehoram, the priests.
verses.17:9: So they taught in Judah, having the Book of the Law of the LORD with them; and they went throughout all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
verses.17:10: And the dread of the LORD fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Judah, so that they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.
verses.17:11: Also some of the Philistines brought gifts and silver as tribute to Jehoshaphat, and the Arabians likewise brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
verses.17:12: So Jehoshaphat continued to grow exceedingly great, and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah.
verses.17:13: And he had abundant stores in the cities of Judah, and men of war, mighty men of valor, in Jerusalem.
verses.17:14: These were their enrollments according to their fathers' houses: Of Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valor;
verses.17:15: and next to him was Jehohanan the commander, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand;
verses.17:16: and next to him was Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself to the LORD, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor.
verses.17:17: And of Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valor, and with him two hundred thousand men armed with bow and shield;
verses.17:18: and next to him was Jehozabad, and with him one hundred and eighty thousand equipped for war.
verses.17:19: These were those who served the king, besides those whom the king had stationed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.
verses.18:1: Now Jehoshaphat had wealth and honor in abundance, and he allied himself by marriage with Ahab.
verses.18:2: After some years he went down to Ahab at Samaria; and Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle in abundance for him and for the people who were with him, and persuaded him to go up against Ramoth Gilead.
verses.18:3: So Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me against Ramoth Gilead?" And he answered him, "I am as you are, and my people as your people; we will be with you in the war."
verses.18:4: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please inquire this day for the word of the LORD."
verses.18:5: Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall we go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I refrain?" And they said, "Go up, for God will deliver it into the hand of the king."
verses.18:6: But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of him?"
verses.18:7: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man by whom we may inquire of the LORD; yet I hate him, because he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil all his days. He is Micaiah the son of Imla." And Jehoshaphat said, "Do not let the king say so."
verses.18:8: Then the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah the son of Imla quickly."
verses.18:9: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah, each arrayed in his robes, were sitting each on his throne; and they were sitting at a threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.18:10: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made horns of iron for himself, and he said, "Thus says the LORD: 'With these you shall gore the Syrians until they are completely destroyed.'"
verses.18:11: And all the prophets prophesied likewise, saying, "Go up to Ramoth Gilead and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king."
verses.18:12: Then the messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Behold, the words of the prophets with one voice declare good to the king. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak favorably."
verses.18:13: And Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, whatever my God says, that I will speak."
verses.18:14: When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I refrain?" And he said, "Go up and prosper, and they will be given into your hand."
verses.18:15: So the king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear that you speak to me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"
verses.18:16: Then he said, "I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These have no master; let each return to his house in peace.'"
verses.18:17: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but only evil?"
verses.18:18: Then he said, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting upon His throne, and all the host of heaven standing on His right hand and on His left.
verses.18:19: And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead?' So one spoke in this manner, and another spoke in that manner.
verses.18:20: Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD, and said, 'I will entice him.' And the LORD said to him, 'By what means?'
verses.18:21: And he said, 'I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And He said, 'You shall entice him, and you shall also prevail; go out and do so.'
verses.18:22: Now therefore, behold, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours, and the LORD has spoken disaster against you."
verses.18:23: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek, and said, "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak to you?"
verses.18:24: And Micaiah said, "Behold, you shall see on that day when you go into an inner chamber to hide yourself."
verses.18:25: Then the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah, and return him to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,
verses.18:26: and say, 'Thus says the king: Put this man in prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and water of affliction, until I return in peace.'"
verses.18:27: But Micaiah said, "If you indeed return in peace, the LORD has not spoken by me." And he said, "Hear, all you peoples!"
verses.18:28: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.
verses.18:29: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and enter into the battle, but you put on your robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into the battle.
verses.18:30: Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of his chariots, saying, "Do not fight with small or great, but only with the king of Israel alone."
verses.18:31: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, "It is the king of Israel!" Therefore they turned aside against him to fight; but Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him, and God drew them away from him.
verses.18:32: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from pursuing him.
verses.18:33: Now a certain man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. So he said to the charioteer, "Turn your hand around and take me out of the host, for I am wounded."
verses.18:34: And the battle grew fiercer that day, and the king of Israel remained propped up in his chariot facing the Syrians until the evening; and about the time of sunset he died.
verses.19:1: Then Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned in peace to his house in Jerusalem.
verses.19:2: Then Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went forth to meet him, and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Ought you to aid the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, wrath is upon you from before the LORD.
verses.19:3: Nevertheless, good things are found in you, in that you have purged the Asherah poles from the land and have set your heart to seek God."
verses.19:4: So Jehoshaphat dwelt in Jerusalem; and he went out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.19:5: Then he appointed judges in the land throughout all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.
verses.19:6: And he said to the judges, "Consider what you are doing, for you do not judge for man but for the LORD, and He is with you in the matter of judgment.
verses.19:7: Now therefore, let the fear of the LORD be upon you; take heed and act carefully, for there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, nor partiality, nor taking of bribes."
verses.19:8: Moreover, in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and the priests, and some of the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, for the judgment of the LORD and for controversies; and they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.19:9: And he commanded them, saying, "Thus you shall act in the fear of the LORD, in faithfulness and with a whole heart:
verses.19:10: Whatever dispute comes before you from your brethren who dwell in their cities, between bloodshed and bloodshed, between law and commandment, statutes and ordinances, you shall warn them, lest they incur guilt before the LORD and wrath come upon you and your brethren. Act thus, and you shall not incur guilt.
verses.19:11: And behold, Amariah the chief priest is over you in every matter of the LORD; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, in every matter of the king; and the Levites shall serve as officers before you. Be strong and act, and may the LORD be with the good."
verses.20:1: Now it came to pass after this that the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Ammonites, came against Jehoshaphat to battle.
verses.20:2: Then some came and reported to Jehoshaphat, saying, "A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram; and behold, they are in Hazazon Tamar, which is En Gedi."
verses.20:3: And Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he set his face to seek the LORD and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
verses.20:4: So Judah assembled to seek help from the LORD; indeed, from all the cities of Judah they came to seek the LORD.
verses.20:5: Then Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court,
verses.20:6: and said, "O LORD, God of our fathers, are You not God in heaven, and do You not rule over all the kingdoms of the nations? In Your hand are power and might, so that none can stand against You.
verses.20:7: Did You not, O our God, dispossess the inhabitants of this land before Your people Israel, and give it to the seed of Abraham Your friend forever?
verses.20:8: And they dwelt in it, and built You a sanctuary in it for Your name, saying,
verses.20:9: 'If calamity comes upon us—sword, judgment, pestilence, or famine—we will stand before this house and before You, for Your name is in this house, and we will cry out to You in our distress, and You will hear and save.'
verses.20:10: And now, behold, the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom You did not permit Israel to invade when they came from the land of Egypt, for they turned aside from them and did not destroy them—
verses.20:11: behold, they are repaying us by coming to cast us out of Your possession which You have given us to inherit.
verses.20:12: O our God, will You not judge them? For we have no strength before this great multitude that is coming against us; neither do we know what to do, but our eyes are upon You."
verses.20:13: Now all Judah stood before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
verses.20:14: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly.
verses.20:15: And he said, "Give ear, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! Thus says the LORD to you: 'Do not fear nor be dismayed before this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God's.
verses.20:16: Tomorrow go down against them. Behold, they are ascending by the Ascent of Ziz, and you shall find them at the end of the valley, before the wilderness of Jeruel.
verses.20:17: It is not for you to fight in this battle; take your stand, stand firm, and behold the salvation of the LORD on your behalf, O Judah and Jerusalem. Do not fear nor be dismayed; tomorrow go out against them, for the LORD is with you.'"
verses.20:18: Then Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before the LORD, worshiping the LORD.
verses.20:19: And the Levites of the sons of the Kohathites and of the sons of the Korahites stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with a voice exceedingly loud.
verses.20:20: So they rose early in the morning and went forth to the wilderness of Tekoa; and as they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Hear me, O Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Put your trust in the LORD your God, and you shall be established; believe His prophets, and you shall prosper."
verses.20:21: And when he had taken counsel with the people, he appointed singers to the LORD and those who would offer praise in the splendor of holiness, going out before the armed men and saying, "Give thanks to the LORD, for His lovingkindness endures forever."
verses.20:22: Now at the time they began with joyful song and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the sons of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah, and they were routed.
verses.20:23: For the sons of Ammon and Moab rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to utterly annihilate and destroy them; and when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Seir, every man helped to destroy his fellow.
verses.20:24: And when Judah came to the watchtower overlooking the wilderness, they turned toward the multitude, and behold, there were corpses fallen to the ground, and not one had escaped.
verses.20:25: When Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoil, they found among them in abundance—goods, corpses, and precious articles—which they stripped off for themselves until they could carry no more; and they spent three days gathering the spoil, for it was exceedingly great.
verses.20:26: And on the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Berachah, for there they blessed the LORD; therefore they called the name of that place the Valley of Berachah to this day.
verses.20:27: Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem returned, with Jehoshaphat at their head, to go back to Jerusalem with joy, for the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.
verses.20:28: So they came to Jerusalem with harps, lyres, and trumpets, to the house of the LORD.
verses.20:29: And the dread of God fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
verses.20:30: Thus the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was quiet, for his God gave him rest all around.
verses.20:31: So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
verses.20:32: And he walked in the way of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the sight of the LORD.
verses.20:33: Nevertheless the high places were not removed, for as yet the people had not directed their hearts to the God of their fathers.
verses.20:34: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, behold, they are written in the records of Jehu the son of Hanani, which were entered into the Book of the Kings of Israel.
verses.20:35: After this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah allied himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.
verses.20:36: He joined with him to build ships to go to Tarshish, and they built ships in Ezion Geber.
verses.20:37: Then Eliezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has shattered your works." And the ships were wrecked, so that they were unable to go to Tarshish.
verses.21:1: And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of David; and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
verses.21:2: Now he had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah; all these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
verses.21:3: And their father gave them abundant gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, together with fortified cities in Judah; but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
verses.21:4: Now when Jehoram had risen over the kingdom of his father and strengthened himself, he slew all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel.
verses.21:5: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.21:6: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
verses.21:7: Yet the LORD was unwilling to destroy the house of David, for the sake of the covenant that He had made with David, and since He had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons for all days.
verses.21:8: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and set a king over themselves.
verses.21:9: So Jehoram crossed over with his officers and all his chariots with him; and rising by night, he struck down the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots.
verses.21:10: Thus Edom has been in revolt from under the hand of Judah to this day. At that same time Libnah also revolted from under his hand, because he had forsaken the LORD, the God of his fathers.
verses.21:11: Moreover, he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit harlotry, and led Judah astray.
verses.21:12: And a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, "Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah,
verses.21:13: but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have caused Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit harlotry like the harlotry of the house of Ahab, and have also slain your brothers of your father's house, who were better than you—
verses.21:14: behold, the LORD will strike your people, your sons, your wives, and all your possessions with a great plague;
verses.21:15: and you yourself shall be afflicted with severe sickness, with a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the sickness, day after day."
verses.21:16: Moreover, the LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabians who bordered the Cushites.
verses.21:17: And they came up against Judah and broke into it, and carried away all the possessions found in the king's house, together with his sons and his wives, so that not a son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
verses.21:18: And after all this the LORD struck him in his bowels with an incurable disease.
verses.21:19: And it came to pass in the course of time, at the end of two years, that his bowels came out because of his disease, and he died in grievous afflictions; and his people made no burning for him, like the burning for his fathers.
verses.21:20: He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He departed with no one's regret; and they buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
verses.22:1: Then the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, his youngest son, king in his place, for the band of raiders that had come with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the older sons. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
verses.22:2: Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
verses.22:3: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in acting wickedly.
verses.22:4: Therefore he did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, like the house of Ahab; for they were his counselors after the death of his father, to his own destruction.
verses.22:5: He also walked in their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth Gilead; and the Arameans wounded Joram.
verses.22:6: And he returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds which they had inflicted upon him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to visit Jehoram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.
verses.22:7: Now the downfall of Ahaziah came from God through his going to Joram; for when he arrived, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
verses.22:8: And it came to pass, when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, that he found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who attended Ahaziah, and he slew them.
verses.22:9: Then he searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria, and brought him to Jehu, and put him to death; yet they buried him, for they said, "He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." So the house of Ahaziah had no one with strength to hold the kingdom.
verses.22:10: Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal seed of the house of Judah.
verses.22:11: But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being slain, and placed him and his nurse in a bedchamber. Thus Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram and wife of Jehoiada the priest—for she was the sister of Ahaziah—hid him from Athaliah, so that she did not slay him.
verses.22:12: And he was hidden with them in the house of God for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.
verses.23:1: And in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds—Azariah the son of Jeroham, Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri—into covenant with him.
verses.23:2: And they went about through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel; and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.23:3: Then all the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said to them, "Behold, the king's son shall reign, just as the LORD spoke concerning the sons of David.
