verses.23:4: This is the thing that you shall do: one-third of you who come in on the Sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, shall be gatekeepers of the thresholds;
verses.23:5: and one-third shall be at the king's house, and one-third at the Gate of the Foundation; and all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the LORD.
verses.23:6: But let no one enter the house of the LORD except the priests and those of the Levites who minister; they may enter, for they are holy, while all the people shall keep the charge of the LORD.
verses.23:7: And the Levites shall surround the king on every side, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whoever enters the house shall be put to death. And be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."
verses.23:8: So the Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest had commanded. And each took his men, those who were coming in on the Sabbath together with those who were going out on the Sabbath; for Jehoiada the priest had not dismissed the divisions.
verses.23:9: And Jehoiada the priest gave to the captains of hundreds the spears, the bucklers, and the shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of God.
verses.23:10: And he stationed all the people, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and by the house, all around the king.
verses.23:11: Then they brought out the king's son, put the crown on him, gave him the testimony, and made him king. And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and declared, "Long live the king!"
verses.23:12: Now when Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people in the house of the LORD.
verses.23:13: And she looked, and behold, the king was standing by his pillar at the entrance, and the princes and the trumpeters were beside the king; and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets, along with the singers with musical instruments and those who led the praise. Then Athaliah tore her garments and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"
verses.23:14: Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds who were appointed over the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever follows her shall be slain with the sword." For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death in the house of the LORD."
verses.23:15: So they laid hands on her; and when she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate at the king's house, they put her to death there.
verses.23:16: Then Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king, that they should be the people of the LORD.
verses.23:17: And all the people went to the house of Baal and tore it down; they broke its altars and its images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.
verses.23:18: Moreover Jehoiada committed the oversight of the house of the LORD into the hand of the Levitical priests, whom David had assigned over the house of the LORD to offer the burnt offerings of the LORD, as it is written in the Law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, according to the direction of David.
verses.23:19: And he stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, so that no one who was unclean in any matter should enter.
verses.23:20: Then he took the captains of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of the LORD; and they entered through the Upper Gate into the king's house, and seated the king upon the throne of the kingdom.
verses.23:21: So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; for they had put Athaliah to death with the sword.
verses.24:1: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
verses.24:2: And Joash did what was right in the sight of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
verses.24:3: And Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.24:4: Now it came to pass after this that Joash purposed in his heart to restore the house of the LORD.
verses.24:5: Then he gathered the priests and the Levites, and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah, and gather silver from all Israel to repair the house of your God from year to year, and hasten to do this matter." Yet the Levites did not hasten.
verses.24:6: So the king called for Jehoiada the chief, and said to him, "Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and from Jerusalem the levy of Moses the servant of the LORD, and of the assembly of Israel, for the Tent of the Testimony?"
verses.24:7: For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of God, and had also devoted all the holy things of the house of the LORD to the Baals.
verses.24:8: Then the king commanded, and they made a chest and placed it outside at the gate of the house of the LORD.
verses.24:9: And they made a proclamation throughout Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the levy that Moses the servant of God had laid upon Israel in the wilderness.
verses.24:10: Then all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and brought their contributions and cast them into the chest until it was full.
verses.24:11: So it came to pass, whenever the chest was brought to the king's office by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that there was much silver, that the king's scribe and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, and carry it back and restore it to its place. Thus they did day by day, and gathered silver in abundance.
verses.24:12: And the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who carried out the work of the service of the house of the LORD; and they hired stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, as well as craftsmen in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.
verses.24:13: So the workmen labored, and the work of restoration went forward in their hands; and they set the house of God according to its original design and strengthened it.
verses.24:14: And when they had finished, they brought the remainder of the silver before the king and Jehoiada, and from it were made utensils for the house of the LORD—utensils for ministering and for offering, spoons, and vessels of gold and silver. And they offered burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually all the days of Jehoiada.
verses.24:15: Now Jehoiada grew old and was full of days, and he died; he was one hundred and thirty years old at his death.
verses.24:16: And they buried him in the City of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God and toward His house.
verses.24:17: Now after the death of Jehoiada, the princes of Judah came and bowed down to the king; and the king listened to them.
verses.24:18: And they forsook the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherah poles and the idols; and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem because of this guilt of theirs.
verses.24:19: Yet He sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD; and they testified against them, but they would not give ear.
verses.24:20: Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, who stood above the people and said to them, "Thus says God: 'Why do you transgress the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has also forsaken you.'"
verses.24:21: So they conspired against him, and by the command of the king they stoned him with stones in the court of the house of the LORD.
verses.24:22: Thus King Joash did not remember the lovingkindness that Jehoiada his father had shown him, but slew his son. And as he was dying, he said, "May the LORD see and require it!"
verses.24:23: And it came to pass at the turn of the year that the army of Syria marched up against him; and they entered Judah and Jerusalem, destroyed all the princes of the people from among the people, and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.
verses.24:24: For though the army of Syria had come with a small company of men, the LORD delivered a very great host into their hand, because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers. Thus they executed judgments upon Joash.
verses.24:25: And when they had departed from him—for they left him in grave afflictions—his own servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed, and he died. So they buried him in the City of David, yet they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
verses.24:26: Now these are the ones who conspired against him: Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonitess, and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith the Moabitess.
verses.24:27: Now concerning his sons, and how great was the oracle against him, and the rebuilding of the house of God, behold, they are written in the commentary of the Book of the Kings. Then Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.25:1: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
verses.25:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, yet not with a whole heart.
verses.25:3: Now it came to pass, as soon as the kingdom was firmly established under him, that he slew his servants who had struck down the king his father.
verses.25:4: Yet he did not put their children to death, but did according to what is written in the Law, in the Book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not die for their children, nor shall children die for their fathers; but every man shall die for his own sin."
verses.25:5: Moreover, Amaziah assembled Judah and set them according to their fathers' houses, under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, throughout all Judah and Benjamin; and he numbered them from twenty years old and upward, and found them to be three hundred thousand chosen men fit to go out to war, able to handle spear and shield.
verses.25:6: He also hired from Israel one hundred thousand mighty men of valor for one hundred talents of silver.
verses.25:7: But a man of God came to him, saying, "O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, nor with any of the sons of Ephraim.
verses.25:8: But if you go—act, be strong for the battle—God will cause you to stumble before the enemy, for God has power to help and to cast down."
verses.25:9: Then Amaziah said to the man of God, "But what is to be done about the one hundred talents which I have given to the troops of Israel?" And the man of God answered, "The LORD is able to give you much more than this."
verses.25:10: So Amaziah separated them, the troop that had come to him from Ephraim, to return to their own place. Therefore their anger was greatly kindled against Judah, and they returned to their own place in fierce anger.
verses.25:11: Then Amaziah took courage and led forth his people, and went to the Valley of Salt, and struck down ten thousand of the sons of Seir.
verses.25:12: Also the sons of Judah captured ten thousand alive, and brought them to the top of the rock, and cast them down from the top of the rock, so that all of them were dashed to pieces.
verses.25:13: But the men of the troop whom Amaziah had sent back from going with him to battle raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria to Beth Horon, struck down three thousand of them, and carried away great spoil.
verses.25:14: Now it came to pass, after Amaziah returned from striking down the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the sons of Seir, set them up as his own gods, bowed down before them, and burned incense to them.
verses.25:15: Therefore the anger of the LORD was kindled against Amaziah, and He sent a prophet to him, who said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of the people, which did not deliver their own people out of your hand?"
verses.25:16: And it came to pass, as he was speaking with him, that the king said to him, "Have we made you the king's counselor? Stop! Why should you be struck down?" Then the prophet stopped, and said, "I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
verses.25:17: Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent to Joash the son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look one another in the face."
verses.25:18: And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as wife.' And a wild beast that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
verses.25:19: You say that you have indeed struck down Edom, and your heart has lifted you up to boast. Now stay at home; why should you provoke calamity, that you should fall, both you and Judah with you?"
verses.25:20: But Amaziah would not listen, for this came from God, in order that He might deliver them into the hand of their enemies, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
verses.25:21: So Joash king of Israel went up; and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked one another in the face at Beth Shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
verses.25:22: And Judah was defeated before Israel, and every man fled to his tent.
verses.25:23: Then Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth Shemesh; and he brought him to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
verses.25:24: And he took all the gold and the silver, all the vessels that were found in the house of God with Obed-Edom, the treasures of the king's house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria.
verses.25:25: And Amaziah the son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Joash the son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
verses.25:26: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, behold, are they not written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel?
verses.25:27: From the time that Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
verses.25:28: And they carried him back on horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of Judah.
verses.26:1: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.26:2: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah, after the king rested with his fathers.
verses.26:3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
verses.26:4: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
verses.26:5: And he continued to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God; and as long as he sought the LORD, God caused him to prosper.
verses.26:6: Now he went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.
verses.26:7: And God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabians who dwelt in Gur Baal, and against the Meunites.
verses.26:8: Also the Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the entrance of Egypt, for he became exceedingly strong.
verses.26:9: Moreover, Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the Angle of the wall, and fortified them.
verses.26:10: He also built towers in the wilderness and hewed out many cisterns, for he had much livestock both in the lowlands and on the plain; and he had farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fertile fields, for he loved the soil.
verses.26:11: Moreover, Uzziah had an army of fighting men who went out to war by divisions, according to the number of their muster made by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
verses.26:12: The whole number of the heads of the fathers' houses among the mighty men of valor was two thousand six hundred.
verses.26:13: And under their command was an army of three hundred seven thousand five hundred men, making war with mighty power to help the king against the enemy.
verses.26:14: And Uzziah provided for them—for the entire army—shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slinging.
verses.26:15: And in Jerusalem he made engines of war, devised by skillful men, to be placed on the towers and on the corners, to shoot arrows and great stones. So his fame spread far abroad, for he was marvelously helped until he became strong.
verses.26:16: But when he became strong, his heart grew proud to his own destruction; and he trespassed against the LORD his God, for he entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense upon the altar of incense.
verses.26:17: And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, men of valor.
verses.26:18: And they withstood King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have trespassed, and this will bring you no honor from the LORD God."
verses.26:19: Then Uzziah became enraged, while holding a censer in his hand to burn incense; and while he was raging against the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead in the presence of the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.
verses.26:20: And Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked upon him, and behold, he was leprous on his forehead; so they hurried him out from there, and indeed he himself hastened to go out, because the LORD had struck him.
verses.26:21: Thus King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death; he dwelt in a separate house as a leper, for he was cut off from the house of the LORD. And Jotham his son was over the king's house, judging the people of the land.
verses.26:22: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, wrote.
verses.26:23: So Uzziah rested with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, "He is a leper." Then Jotham his son reigned in his place.
verses.27:1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok.
verses.27:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah had done, only he did not enter the temple of the LORD. Yet the people still acted corruptly.
verses.27:3: He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and on the wall of Ophel he built extensively.
verses.27:4: Moreover, he built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the forests he built fortresses and towers.
verses.27:5: He also fought with the king of the sons of Ammon and prevailed over them; and the sons of Ammon gave him in that year one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand kors of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. This same amount the sons of Ammon rendered to him in the second year and in the third as well.
verses.27:6: So Jotham grew mighty, because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God.
verses.27:7: Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars and his ways, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.27:9: So Jotham rested with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David. Then Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.28:1: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he did not do what was right in the sight of the LORD, as his father David had done.
verses.28:2: For he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and also made molten images for the Baals.
verses.28:3: He also burned incense in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, and burned his sons in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the children of Israel.
verses.28:4: And he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, upon the hills, and under every green tree.
verses.28:5: Therefore the LORD his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria; and they struck him and carried away from him a great multitude of captives, and brought them to Damascus. He was also delivered into the hand of the king of Israel, who struck him with a great slaughter.
verses.28:6: For Pekah the son of Remaliah slew in Judah one hundred and twenty thousand in one day, all of them valiant men, because they had forsaken the LORD God of their fathers.
verses.28:7: And Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, slew Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the overseer of the house, and Elkanah who was second to the king.
verses.28:8: Then the children of Israel carried away captive from their brethren two hundred thousand—women, sons, and daughters—and also plundered much spoil from them, and brought the spoil to Samaria.
verses.28:9: Now a prophet of the LORD was there, whose name was Oded; and he went out before the army that came to Samaria, and said to them, "Behold, in the wrath of the LORD God of your fathers against Judah, He has delivered them into your hand; yet you have slain them in a fury that has reached up to heaven.
verses.28:10: And now you intend to subdue the children of Judah and Jerusalem to be male and female servants for yourselves; yet do you not yourselves have guilt against the LORD your God?
verses.28:11: Now therefore hear me, and return the captives whom you have taken captive from your brethren, for the fierce wrath of the LORD is upon you."
verses.28:12: Then certain men of the heads of the children of Ephraim—Azariah the son of Johanan, Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai—stood up against those who came from the war,
verses.28:13: and said to them, "You shall not bring the captives in here, for what you intend would bring guilt against the LORD upon us, adding to our sins and to our guilt; for our guilt is great, and fierce wrath is upon Israel."
verses.28:14: So the armed men left the captives and the spoil before the leaders and all the assembly.
verses.28:15: Then the men who were designated by name rose up and took charge of the captives, and from the spoil they clothed all who were naked among them; they dressed them and gave them sandals, fed them and gave them drink, and anointed them; and they conveyed all the feeble ones on donkeys, and brought them to their brethren at Jericho, the city of palm trees. Then they returned to Samaria.
verses.28:16: At that same time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him.
verses.28:17: For again the Edomites had come, struck Judah, and carried away captives.
verses.28:18: The Philistines also had raided the cities of the lowland and of the South of Judah, and had captured Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Socho with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages; and they dwelt there.
verses.28:19: For the LORD humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had cast off restraint in Judah and had dealt most unfaithfully with the LORD.
verses.28:20: And Tilgath-Pilneser king of Assyria came against him and distressed him, and did not strengthen him.
verses.28:21: For Ahaz took a portion from the house of the LORD, from the house of the king, and from the leaders, and gave it to the king of Assyria; yet it was of no help to him.
verses.28:22: Now in the time of his distress he became even more unfaithful to the LORD—this same King Ahaz.
verses.28:23: For he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who had struck him, saying, "Because the gods of the kings of Syria help them, I will sacrifice to them that they may help me." Yet they became the ruin of him and of all Israel.
verses.28:24: So Ahaz gathered the vessels of the house of God, cut in pieces the vessels of the house of God, shut up the doors of the house of the LORD, and made for himself altars in every corner of Jerusalem.
verses.28:25: And in every single city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and provoked to anger the LORD God of his fathers.
verses.28:26: Now the rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.28:27: So Ahaz rested with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem; for they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. Then Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.29:1: Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah the daughter of Zechariah.
verses.29:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father David had done.
verses.29:3: In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
verses.29:4: Then he brought in the priests and the Levites, and gathered them into the East Square,
verses.29:5: and said to them, "Hear me, Levites! Now sanctify yourselves, sanctify the house of the LORD God of your fathers, and carry out the filthiness from the holy place.
verses.29:6: For our fathers have been unfaithful and have done evil in the sight of the LORD our God; they have forsaken Him, have turned their faces away from the dwelling place of the LORD, and have turned their backs.
verses.29:7: They have also shut up the doors of the vestibule, put out the lamps, and have not burned incense or offered burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
verses.29:8: Therefore the wrath of the LORD fell upon Judah and Jerusalem, and He has delivered them up to terror, to desolation, and to hissing, as you see with your own eyes.
verses.29:9: For behold, our fathers have fallen by the sword; and our sons, our daughters, and our wives are in captivity because of this.
verses.29:10: Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD God of Israel, that His fierce wrath may turn away from us.
verses.29:11: My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before Him, to minister to Him, and to be His ministers and burners of incense."
verses.29:12: Then these Levites arose: Mahath the son of Amasai and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites; of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi and Azariah the son of Jehallelel; of the Gershonites, Joah the son of Zimmah and Eden the son of Joah;
verses.29:13: of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel; of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
verses.29:14: of the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
verses.29:15: And they gathered their brethren, sanctified themselves, and went in according to the commandment of the king, at the words of the LORD, to cleanse the house of the LORD.
verses.29:16: Then the priests went into the inner part of the house of the LORD to cleanse it, and brought out all the uncleanness that they found in the temple of the LORD to the court of the house of the LORD. And the Levites took it, to carry it out to the Brook Kidron.
verses.29:17: Now they began to sanctify on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the vestibule of the LORD. So they sanctified the house of the LORD in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
verses.29:18: Then they went inside to King Hezekiah and said, "We have cleansed all the house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the table of the showbread with all its utensils.
verses.29:19: Moreover, all the vessels which King Ahaz in his reign had cast aside in his unfaithfulness we have prepared and sanctified; and behold, they are before the altar of the LORD."
verses.29:20: Then King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the rulers of the city, and went up to the house of the LORD.
verses.29:21: And they brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. Then he commanded the priests, the sons of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the LORD.
verses.29:22: So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and sprinkled it on the altar. Likewise they slaughtered the rams and sprinkled the blood on the altar. They also slaughtered the lambs and sprinkled the blood on the altar.
verses.29:23: Then they brought forward the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands upon them.
verses.29:24: And the priests slaughtered them, and presented their blood as a sin offering on the altar to make atonement for all Israel, for the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering be made for all Israel.
verses.29:25: And he stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, with harps, and with lyres, according to the commandment of David, of Gad the king's seer, and of Nathan the prophet; for thus was the commandment from the LORD through His prophets.
verses.29:26: The Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.
verses.29:27: Then Hezekiah commanded them to offer the burnt offering on the altar. And when the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD also began, with the trumpets and accompanied by the instruments of David king of Israel.
verses.29:28: So all the assembly worshiped, the singers sang, and the trumpets sounded; all this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
verses.29:29: And when they had finished offering, the king and all who were present with him bowed down and worshiped.
verses.29:30: Moreover King Hezekiah and the leaders commanded the Levites to sing praise to the LORD with the words of David and of Asaph the seer. So they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshiped.
verses.29:31: Then Hezekiah answered and said, "Now that you have consecrated yourselves to the LORD, draw near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings into the house of the LORD." So the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and as many as were of a willing heart brought burnt offerings.
verses.29:32: And the number of the burnt offerings which the assembly brought was seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs; all these were for a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.29:33: And the consecrated offerings were six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep.
verses.29:34: Only the priests were too few, so that they could not skin all the burnt offerings; therefore their brethren the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until the priests had sanctified themselves, for the Levites were more upright of heart to sanctify themselves than the priests.
verses.29:35: Also the burnt offerings were in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings and with the drink offerings for every burnt offering. So the service of the house of the LORD was set in order.
verses.29:36: Then Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced over what God had prepared for the people, since the thing had come about suddenly.
verses.30:1: Then Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to observe the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.30:2: For the king and his officials and all the assembly in Jerusalem had taken counsel to observe the Passover in the second month.
verses.30:3: For they were not able to observe it at that time, because the priests had not consecrated themselves in sufficient number, nor had the people gathered together to Jerusalem.
verses.30:4: And the matter was right in the eyes of the king and in the eyes of all the assembly.
verses.30:5: So they established a decree to send a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that they should come to observe the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel, in Jerusalem; for they had not observed it in great numbers as it was written.
verses.30:6: Then the couriers went with the letters from the hand of the king and his officials throughout all Israel and Judah, and according to the commandment of the king, saying, "O children of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, that He may return to the escaped remnant remaining to you from the hand of the kings of Assyria.
verses.30:7: And do not be like your fathers and like your brethren, who acted unfaithfully against the LORD, the God of their fathers, so that He gave them over to desolation, as you see.
verses.30:8: Now do not stiffen your neck as your fathers did; yield your hand to the LORD, and enter His sanctuary, which He has consecrated forever, and serve the LORD your God, that the fierceness of His wrath may turn away from you.
verses.30:9: For if you return to the LORD, your brethren and your children will find compassion before those who led them captive, so that they will return to this land; for the LORD your God is gracious and merciful, and He will not turn His face away from you if you return to Him."
verses.30:10: So the couriers passed from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, even as far as Zebulun, but the people laughed them to scorn and mocked them.
verses.30:11: Nevertheless, some men from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
verses.30:12: Also the hand of God was upon Judah to give them one heart to carry out the commandment of the king and the officials, by the word of the LORD.
verses.30:13: Now a great multitude of people gathered at Jerusalem to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month, an exceedingly great assembly.
verses.30:14: And they arose and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem, and all the incense altars they removed and cast into the Brook Kidron.
verses.30:15: Then they slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. And the priests and the Levites were ashamed, and consecrated themselves, and brought burnt offerings into the house of the LORD.
verses.30:16: They stood in their appointed place according to their ordinance, according to the Law of Moses the man of God; the priests sprinkled the blood received from the hand of the Levites.
verses.30:17: For there were many in the assembly who had not consecrated themselves; therefore the Levites were over the slaughtering of the Passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to consecrate them to the LORD.
verses.30:18: For a multitude of the people, many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet they ate the Passover otherwise than as it was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the good LORD provide atonement for
verses.30:19: everyone who sets his whole heart to seek God, the LORD, the God of his fathers, though not according to the purification of the sanctuary."
verses.30:20: And the LORD listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.
verses.30:21: So the children of Israel who were present in Jerusalem kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with great gladness; and the Levites and the priests praised the LORD day by day with resounding instruments to the LORD.
verses.30:22: And Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good understanding in the service of the LORD. And they ate throughout the feast for the seven days, sacrificing peace offerings and making confession to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.30:23: Then the whole assembly took counsel to observe another seven days, and they observed those seven days with gladness.
verses.30:24: For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed to the assembly one thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the officials contributed to the assembly one thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; and a great number of priests consecrated themselves.
verses.30:25: And the whole assembly of Judah rejoiced, with the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly that came from Israel, and the sojourners who came from the land of Israel and those who dwelt in Judah.
verses.30:26: So there was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, there had been nothing like this in Jerusalem.
verses.30:27: Then the Levitical priests arose and blessed the people, and their voice was heard; and their prayer came to His holy habitation, to heaven.
verses.31:1: Now when all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah and shattered the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and the altars throughout all Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had utterly destroyed them all. Then all the children of Israel returned, every man to his possession, to their own cities.
verses.31:2: And Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites according to their divisions, each man according to his service, both the priests and the Levites, for burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to minister, to give thanks, and to praise in the gates of the camps of the LORD.
verses.31:3: Also the king's portion from his own substance was appointed for the burnt offerings—for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths, the New Moons, and the appointed feasts, as it is written in the Law of the LORD.
verses.31:4: Moreover he commanded the people who dwelt in Jerusalem to give the portion belonging to the priests and the Levites, that they might hold fast to the Law of the LORD.
verses.31:5: As soon as the command spread abroad, the children of Israel gave in abundance the firstfruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and of all the produce of the field; and they brought in the tithe of everything abundantly.
verses.31:6: And the children of Israel and Judah who dwelt in the cities of Judah, they also brought in the tithe of oxen and sheep, and the tithe of the holy things which were consecrated to the LORD their God, and laid them in heaps upon heaps.
verses.31:7: In the third month they began to lay the foundation of the heaps, and in the seventh month they finished.
verses.31:8: When Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, they blessed the LORD and His people Israel.
verses.31:9: Then Hezekiah inquired of the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps.
verses.31:10: And Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, answered him and said, "Since they began to bring the offerings into the house of the LORD, we have eaten and been satisfied and have left over in great abundance; for the LORD has blessed His people, and what is left over is this great store."
verses.31:11: Then Hezekiah commanded them to prepare chambers in the house of the LORD; and they prepared them.
verses.31:12: And they faithfully brought in the offerings, the tithes, and the consecrated things; over them Conaniah the Levite was ruler, and Shimei his brother was second in command.
verses.31:13: And Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were overseers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the ruler of the house of God.
verses.31:14: And Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper at the East Gate, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute the offerings of the LORD and the most holy things.
verses.31:15: And under his hand were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, to distribute faithfully to their brethren by divisions, to the great and the small alike.
verses.31:16: This was apart from those males enrolled by genealogy from three years old and upward, everyone who entered the house of the LORD for his daily portion, for their service in their watches according to their divisions.
verses.31:17: The enrollment of the priests was according to their fathers' houses, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward were enrolled in their watches according to their divisions.
verses.31:18: They were enrolled with all their little ones, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, for the whole assembly; for in their faithfulness they kept themselves consecrated in holiness.
verses.31:19: Also for the sons of Aaron, the priests, who were in the fields of the pasturelands of their cities, in every single city, there were men who were designated by name to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled by genealogy among the Levites.
verses.31:20: Thus Hezekiah did throughout all Judah, and he did what was good and right and true before the LORD his God.
verses.31:21: And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law and in the commandment, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.
verses.32:1: After these deeds and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah; he encamped against the fortified cities, and purposed to breach them for himself.
verses.32:2: And Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come, and that his face was set to make war against Jerusalem.
verses.32:3: Therefore he took counsel with his officers and his mighty men to stop up the waters of the springs that were outside the city, and they helped him.
verses.32:4: So a great multitude gathered together, and they stopped up all the springs and the brook that flowed through the midst of the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find abundant water?"
verses.32:5: And he took courage, and rebuilt all the broken wall and raised it up to the towers, and built another wall outside; he also strengthened the Millo in the City of David, and made weapons and shields in abundance.
verses.32:6: Then he appointed commanders of war over the people, and gathered them to himself in the broad square at the gate of the city, and spoke to their hearts, saying,
verses.32:7: "Be strong and courageous; do not fear nor be dismayed before the king of Assyria, nor before all the multitude that is with him; for there is more with us than with him.
verses.32:8: With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God, to help us and to fight our battles." And the people relied upon the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
verses.32:9: After this Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem—while he himself was before Lachish, and all his imperial power with him—to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying,
verses.32:10: "Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria: Upon what do you place your trust, that you abide under siege in Jerusalem?
verses.32:11: Is not Hezekiah enticing you to give you over to die by famine and by thirst, saying, 'The LORD our God shall deliver us from the grasp of the king of Assyria'?
verses.32:12: Has not this same Hezekiah taken away His high places and His altars, and spoken to Judah and to Jerusalem, saying, 'Before one altar you shall worship, and upon it you shall burn incense'?
verses.32:13: Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands at all able to deliver their land from my hand?
verses.32:14: Who among all the gods of these nations that my fathers utterly destroyed was able to deliver his people from my hand, that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand?
verses.32:15: Now therefore, do not let Hezekiah deceive you, nor mislead you in this manner, and do not believe him; for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers. How much less shall your God deliver you from my hand!"
verses.32:16: And his servants spoke still more against the LORD God and against His servant Hezekiah.
verses.32:17: He also wrote letters to revile the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against Him, saying, "As the gods of the nations of the lands have not delivered their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah shall not deliver His people from my hand."
verses.32:18: Then they called out with a loud voice in the language of Judah to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten them and terrify them, so that they might capture the city.
verses.32:19: And they spoke against the God of Jerusalem as against the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of the hands of man.
verses.32:20: And King Hezekiah and Isaiah the son of Amoz, the prophet, prayed concerning this, and cried out to heaven.
verses.32:21: Then the LORD sent an angel, who cut off every mighty man of valor, leader, and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned in shame of face to his own land; and when he entered the house of his god, some of his own offspring struck him down there with the sword.
verses.32:22: Thus the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria, and from the hand of all others, and guided them on every side.
verses.32:23: And many brought offerings to the LORD at Jerusalem, and precious gifts to Hezekiah king of Judah, so that he was exalted in the sight of all the nations from that time onward.
verses.32:24: In those days Hezekiah fell sick to the point of death; and he prayed to the LORD, and He spoke to him and gave him a sign.
verses.32:25: Yet Hezekiah did not make return according to the favor bestowed upon him, for his heart was lifted up; therefore wrath came upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.32:26: Then Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
verses.32:27: Now Hezekiah had exceedingly great riches and honor; and he made for himself treasuries for silver, for gold, for precious stones, for spices, for shields, and for all kinds of precious articles,
verses.32:28: storehouses also for the yield of grain, new wine, and oil, and stalls for every kind of livestock, and flocks for the folds.
verses.32:29: Moreover he provided cities for himself, and possessions of flocks and herds in abundance; for God had given him very great wealth.
verses.32:30: This same Hezekiah also stopped up the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon, and directed them straight down to the west side of the City of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all his works.
verses.32:31: Yet in the matter of the envoys of the princes of Babylon, who were sent to him to inquire about the sign that had occurred in the land, God left him to himself to test him, that He might know all that was in his heart.
verses.32:32: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and his deeds of devotion, behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, the prophet, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.32:33: So Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem rendered honor to him at his death. Then Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
verses.33:1: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
verses.33:2: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the children of Israel.
verses.33:3: For he rebuilt the high places which Hezekiah his father had torn down; he raised up altars for the Baals, and made Asherah poles, and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
verses.33:4: He also built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem shall My name be forever."
verses.33:5: And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.
verses.33:6: He also caused his sons to pass through the fire in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom; he practiced soothsaying, used divination, practiced sorcery, and appointed mediums and spiritists. He did much evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.33:7: And he set the carved image of the idol which he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever;
verses.33:8: and I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the land which I have appointed for your fathers, if only they take care to do all that I have commanded them, according to all the law and the statutes and the ordinances given by the hand of Moses."
verses.33:9: Thus Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray, so that they did more evil than the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the children of Israel.
verses.33:10: And the LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, yet they did not pay heed.
verses.33:11: Therefore the LORD brought upon them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, who captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze fetters, and led him away to Babylon.
verses.33:12: And when he was in distress, he implored the favor of the LORD his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.
verses.33:13: And he prayed to Him; and He was moved by his plea, and heard his supplication, and brought him back to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD, He is God.
verses.33:14: Now after this he built an outer wall for the City of David on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, extending to the entrance of the Fish Gate; and he encircled Ophel and raised it to a very great height. He also stationed commanders of the army in all the fortified cities of Judah.
verses.33:15: And he removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and cast them outside the city.
verses.33:16: He also rebuilt the altar of the LORD, and sacrificed upon it peace offerings and thank offerings, and commanded Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.33:17: Nevertheless the people still sacrificed on the high places, yet only to the LORD their God.
verses.33:18: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, behold, they are in the Acts of the Kings of Israel.
verses.33:19: Also his prayer, and how God responded to his plea, and all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and set up the Asherah poles and the carved images before he humbled himself, behold, they are written in the records of Hozai.
verses.33:20: So Manasseh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house. Then Amon his son reigned in his place.
verses.33:21: Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
verses.33:22: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, as Manasseh his father had done; for Amon sacrificed to all the carved images which Manasseh his father had made, and served them.
verses.33:23: And he did not humble himself before the LORD, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; rather, this same Amon multiplied his guilt.
verses.33:24: Then his servants conspired against him, and put him to death in his own house.
verses.33:25: But the people of the land struck down all those who had conspired against King Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
verses.34:1: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
verses.34:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the ways of his father David; he did not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.
verses.34:3: For in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of his father David; and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherah poles, the carved images, and the molded images.
verses.34:4: They broke down the altars of the Baals in his presence, and the incense altars that stood high above them he cut down; and the Asherah poles, the carved images, and the molded images he shattered and ground to dust, and scattered it upon the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
verses.34:5: He also burned the bones of the priests upon their altars, and purged Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.34:6: And so he did in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, even as far as Naphtali, in their ruined places all around.
verses.34:7: He tore down the altars and beat the Asherah poles and the carved images into powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel; then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.34:8: Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, while purging the land and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair the house of the LORD his God.
verses.34:9: When they came to Hilkiah the high priest, they delivered the money that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites, the keepers of the threshold, had gathered from the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin; and they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.34:10: And they placed it in the hand of the workmen who had the oversight of the house of the LORD; and the workmen who labored in the house of the LORD gave it to mend and repair the house.
verses.34:11: They gave it to the craftsmen and builders to buy quarried stone, and timber for couplings and to make beams for the chambers that the kings of Judah had destroyed.
verses.34:12: And the men did the work faithfully. Appointed over them to oversee it were Jahath and Obadiah the Levites, of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, along with the Levites, all of whom were skilled with instruments of music.
verses.34:13: They were also over the burden bearers and directed all who did the work in every kind of service; and some of the Levites were scribes, officers, and gatekeepers.
verses.34:14: Now while they were bringing out the money that had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the Book of the Law of the LORD given by the hand of Moses.
verses.34:15: Then Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD." And Hilkiah delivered the book to Shaphan.
verses.34:16: So Shaphan brought the book to the king, and moreover he brought the king word, saying, "All that was committed to the hand of your servants, they are doing.
verses.34:17: And they have emptied out the money that was found in the house of the LORD, and have delivered it into the hand of the overseers and into the hand of the workmen."
verses.34:18: Then Shaphan the scribe informed the king, saying, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read from it before the king.
verses.34:19: And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the Law, that he tore his garments.
verses.34:20: Then the king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king's servant, saying,
verses.34:21: "Go, inquire of the LORD for me, and for those who remain in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the book that has been found; for great is the wrath of the LORD that has been poured out upon us, because our fathers have not kept the word of the LORD, to do according to all that is written in this book."
verses.34:22: So Hilkiah and those whom the king had appointed went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe—now she dwelt in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter—and they spoke to her concerning this matter.
verses.34:23: And she said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to me,
verses.34:24: 'Thus says the LORD: Behold, I am bringing calamity upon this place and upon its inhabitants, even all the curses that are written in the book which they have read before the king of Judah,
verses.34:25: because they have forsaken Me and have burned incense to other gods, that they might provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands; therefore My wrath shall be poured out upon this place, and it shall not be quenched.'
verses.34:26: But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD, thus you shall say to him: 'Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the words which you have heard:
verses.34:27: Because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before God when you heard His words against this place and against its inhabitants, and humbled yourself before Me, and tore your garments and wept before Me, I also have heard you, declares the LORD.
verses.34:28: Behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace; and your eyes shall not see all the calamity that I am bringing upon this place and upon its inhabitants.'" So they brought back word to the king.
verses.34:29: Then the king sent and gathered together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.34:30: And the king went up to the house of the LORD, with all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem—the priests and the Levites, and all the people, both great and small—and he read in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.
verses.34:31: Then the king stood in his place and made a covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and to keep His commandments and His testimonies and His statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to perform the words of the covenant that were written in this book.
verses.34:32: And he made all who were present in Jerusalem and Benjamin take a stand in it. So the inhabitants of Jerusalem acted according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.
verses.34:33: Thus Josiah removed all the abominations from all the territories that belonged to the children of Israel, and caused all who were present in Israel to serve the LORD their God. All his days they did not turn aside from following the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.35:1: Now Josiah kept a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.35:2: And he appointed the priests to their duties and encouraged them for the service of the house of the LORD.
verses.35:3: Then he said to the Levites who taught all Israel, who were consecrated to the LORD, "Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, built; it is no longer a burden upon your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and His people Israel.
verses.35:4: Prepare yourselves according to your fathers' houses, by your divisions, following the written instruction of David king of Israel and the written record of Solomon his son.
verses.35:5: And stand in the sanctuary according to the groupings of the fathers' houses of your brethren, the lay people, with a division of a Levite father's house assigned to each.
verses.35:6: So slaughter the Passover lambs, consecrate yourselves, and prepare them for your brethren, that they may do according to the word of the LORD given by the hand of Moses."
verses.35:7: Then Josiah contributed to the lay people, for all who were present, flocks of lambs and young goats—all for the Passover offerings—to the number of thirty thousand, and three thousand cattle; these were from the king's possessions.
verses.35:8: And his officials contributed willingly to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, rulers of the house of God, gave to the priests for the Passover offerings two thousand six hundred small livestock and three hundred cattle.
verses.35:9: Also Conaniah, and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jozabad, chiefs of the Levites, contributed to the Levites for the Passover offerings five thousand small livestock and five hundred cattle.
verses.35:10: So the service was prepared, and the priests stood in their places, and the Levites in their divisions, according to the king's command.
verses.35:11: And they slaughtered the Passover lambs; and the priests sprinkled the blood that they received from their hands, while the Levites skinned the animals.
verses.35:12: Then they set aside the burnt offerings to distribute them according to the groupings of the fathers' houses of the lay people, to offer to the LORD, as it is written in the Book of Moses. And so they did with the cattle.
verses.35:13: Also they roasted the Passover offerings with fire according to the ordinance; and the other holy offerings they boiled in pots, in cauldrons, and in pans, and carried them swiftly to all the lay people.
verses.35:14: Afterward they made preparation for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were occupied in offering the burnt offerings and the fat portions until night; therefore the Levites made preparation for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.
verses.35:15: And the singers, the sons of Asaph, were in their places, according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's seer; and the gatekeepers were at every gate. They did not need to depart from their service, because their brethren the Levites made preparation for them.
verses.35:16: So all the service of the LORD was prepared on that day, to keep the Passover and to offer burnt offerings upon the altar of the LORD, according to the command of King Josiah.
verses.35:17: And the children of Israel who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
verses.35:18: No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet; nor had any of the kings of Israel ever kept such a Passover as Josiah kept, with the priests and the Levites, all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.35:19: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah this Passover was kept.
verses.35:20: After all this, when Josiah had prepared the temple, Necho king of Egypt came up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates; and Josiah went out against him.
verses.35:21: But he sent messengers to him, saying, "What have I to do with you, O king of Judah? I am not coming against you this day, but against the house with which I am at war; and God has commanded me to make haste. Refrain from opposing God, who is with me, lest He destroy you."
verses.35:22: Nevertheless Josiah would not turn his face from him, but disguised himself so that he might fight against him, and did not heed the words of Necho from the mouth of God. So he came to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
verses.35:23: And the archers shot King Josiah; and the king said to his servants, "Take me away, for I am severely wounded."
verses.35:24: His servants therefore took him out of that chariot and placed him in the second chariot that he had, and they brought him to Jerusalem. So he died, and was buried in the tombs of his fathers. And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
verses.35:25: Jeremiah also lamented for Josiah. And to this day all the singing men and the singing women speak of Josiah in their laments. They made them an ordinance in Israel; and behold, they are written in the Laments.
verses.35:26: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and his deeds of devotion, according to what is written in the Law of the LORD,
verses.35:27: and his deeds from first to last, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.36:1: Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and enthroned him as king in place of his father in Jerusalem.
verses.36:2: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years of age when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
verses.36:3: Now the king of Egypt deposed him at Jerusalem, and exacted a fine upon the land of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
verses.36:4: Then the king of Egypt appointed Eliakim his brother as king over Judah and Jerusalem, and altered his name to Jehoiakim; and Necho seized Jehoahaz his brother and brought him away to Egypt.
verses.36:5: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years of age when he came to the throne, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD his God.
verses.36:6: Against him marched up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and bound him in bronze fetters to lead him away to Babylon.
verses.36:7: Nebuchadnezzar also carried some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon, and placed them within his own temple in Babylon.
verses.36:8: Now the remainder of the deeds of Jehoiakim, and the abominations which he committed, and that which was found against him, behold, they are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. Then Jehoiachin his son reigned in his stead.
verses.36:9: Jehoiachin was eight years of age when he came to the throne, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem; and he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD.
verses.36:10: At the turning of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar sent and had him brought to Babylon, together with the precious vessels of the house of the LORD, and appointed Zedekiah his brother as king over Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.36:11: Zedekiah was twenty-one years of age when he came to the throne, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
verses.36:12: He did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD his God, and did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.
verses.36:13: Furthermore, he rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had required him to swear by God; and he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against returning to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.36:14: Moreover, all the chief officers of the priests and the people multiplied their unfaithful transgressions, following all the abominations of the nations; and they defiled the house of the LORD which He had consecrated in Jerusalem.
verses.36:15: Yet the LORD, the God of their fathers, sent warnings to them by the hand of His messengers, rising early and sending again and again, for He had compassion upon His people and upon His dwelling place.
verses.36:16: But they continually mocked the messengers of God, despised His words, and scoffed at His prophets, until the wrath of the LORD mounted against His people, until there remained no remedy.
verses.36:17: Therefore He brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, who slew their young men with the sword within the house of their sanctuary, and spared neither young man nor maiden, neither the aged nor the frail; He delivered them all into his hand.
verses.36:18: And all the vessels of the house of God, both great and small, together with the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king and of his princes—all of these he carried away to Babylon.
verses.36:19: They set fire to the house of God, tore down the wall of Jerusalem, consumed all its palaces with fire, and reduced all its prized articles to ruin.
verses.36:20: And those who remained as a remnant from the sword he led into exile to Babylon, where they became servants to him and to his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia,
verses.36:21: in fulfillment of the word of the LORD through the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed its sabbaths; throughout all the days of its desolation it kept sabbath, until seventy years were completed.
verses.36:22: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be brought to completion, the LORD roused the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he sent a proclamation throughout his entire realm and set it down in writing as well, declaring:
verses.36:23: "Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: The LORD, the God of heaven, has bestowed upon me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has charged me to build a house for Him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever is among you of all His people, may the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up."

notes.1:5: The Masoretic vocalization reads 'was there' (sham). The Hebrew object suffix rendered 'Him' in 'sought Him' may refer either to the LORD or to the bronze altar before the tabernacle.
notes.1:13: The Masoretic Text has the preposition 'to/at' on 'the high place' (rendered locatively 'at the high place'), whereas several ancient versions read 'from the high place.'
notes.1:16: Kue (Hebrew Qeveh) refers to Cilicia in southeastern Anatolia, a region renowned in antiquity for horse breeding and trade.
notes.2:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, chapter 2 begins at this verse (corresponding to 2:2 in many English translations, while 1:18 corresponds to 2:1).
notes.2:9: A kor was a dry measure of roughly six bushels (about 220 liters), and a bath was a liquid measure of roughly six gallons (about 22 liters).
notes.2:12: Huram-Abi literally means 'Huram my father,' using 'father' as an honorific title for a master craftsman or chief artisan (cf. 2 Chronicles 4:16).
notes.3:4: The Masoretic Text explicitly records the height of the vestibule as one hundred and twenty cubits; some ancient versions read twenty cubits.
notes.3:10: The Hebrew term rendered 'sculpted work' (tsaatsuim) occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes carved or sculpted imagery.
notes.3:16: Hebrew baddebir literally means 'in the inner sanctuary' and is sometimes interpreted as 'as in the inner sanctuary' or 'like a necklace.'
notes.3:17: The ketiv and qere on 'the one on the right' differ only in spelling (with or without an internal yod). Jachin means 'He shall establish,' and Boaz means 'in Him is strength.'
notes.4:3: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "oxen" here, whereas the parallel account in 1 Kings 7:24 describes ornamental "gourds" beneath the rim of the Sea.
notes.4:5: The Hebrew pairs two verbs of capacity to state that the molten Sea could hold three thousand baths, likely indicating full brim capacity alongside the two thousand baths of 1 Kings 7:26.
notes.4:11: Following the traditional reading (Qere) "Huram," matching the first occurrence in the verse; the written consonantal text (Ketiv) spells the name "Hiram."
notes.4:16: Literally "Huram his father," an honorific title denoting a master craftsman or chief artisan (compare 2 Chronicles 2:13).
notes.5:5: The Hebrew text places "the priests" and "the Levites" in apposition without a conjunction, designating the Levitical priests.
notes.5:9: The Hebrew verb is singular ("it remains"), referring to the ark resting in its place at the time the original royal record was written.
notes.5:12: Following the traditional reading (Qere) for the participle "blowing" rather than the written consonantal spelling (Ketiv) with a repeated consonant.
notes.5:13: Following the traditional reading (Qere) for "the trumpeters" rather than the written consonantal spelling (Ketiv) with an extra consonant.
notes.6:13: The Hebrew phrase kiyor nechoshet literally refers to a bronze basin-shaped dais or platform; five cubits by five cubits and three cubits high corresponds to roughly seven and a half feet square and four and a half feet high.
notes.6:26: The phrase when You afflict them follows the traditional sense of divine discipline through drought, though the Masoretic vocalization of the Hebrew verb can also be read as when You answer them.
notes.6:42: The mercies of Your servant David translates Hebrew chasdei Dawid, referring to the steadfast covenant promises and lovingkindnesses pledged to David, echoing Psalm 132:8-10.
notes.7:6: The Masoretic Text has a ketiv/qere orthographic variant on the participle for sounding trumpets, with the ketiv spelling the form with a doubled tsade and the qere reading the standard Hiphil participle; both carry the same meaning and the qere is translated.
notes.7:14: Upon whom My name is called renders the Hebrew idiom of covenant ownership, and I Myself reflects the emphatic Hebrew subject pronoun introducing the divine response.
notes.7:20: The Masoretic Hebrew shifts from the second-person plural in verse 19 to the third-person plural (them) here when pronouncing the judgment of exile upon the nation.
notes.8:10: Follows the Qere reading (hannitsavim, 'those stationed' or 'chief officers'); the Ketiv writes the plural noun form (hanetsivim, 'prefects' or 'deputies') with the same basic sense.
notes.8:16: Literally 'up to the day of the foundation of the house of the LORD and until its completion,' encompassing both the preparatory work before the foundation was laid and the building work until it was finished.
notes.8:18: Follows the Qere orthographic form ('oniyyot, 'ships') rather than the plene Ketiv spelling.
notes.9:4: The Hebrew reads 'his ascent' ('aliyyato, referring to the royal stairway or processional way leading up to the temple), whereas the parallel passage in 1 Kings 10:5 reads 'his burnt offering.'
notes.9:10: Follows the Qere spelling 'Huram,' consistent with Chronicles; the Ketiv writes 'Hiram,' the form used in Kings.
notes.9:12: The Hebrew phrase 'besides what she had brought to the king' is elliptical, indicating gifts given in addition to a royal return matching the tribute she had presented.
notes.9:29: Follows the Qere form 'Yeddo' (traditionally spelled 'Iddo' in English); the Ketiv writes 'Yedi.'
notes.10:14: The Masoretic Text of Chronicles reads the first-person verb 'I will make your yoke heavy' ('akhbid), whereas 1 Kings 12:14 reads 'My father made your yoke heavy.'
notes.10:16: The Hebrew of Chronicles opens with an elliptical clause omitting an explicit verb such as 'saw' (unlike 1 Kings 12:16), moving directly from 'all Israel' and the king's refusal to the people's reply.
notes.11:15: The Hebrew word translated goat idols literally means hairy ones or satyrs, referring to pagan goat-shaped deities.
notes.11:18: The Ketiv reads son, while the Qere followed here reads daughter; Abihail is introduced without a conjunction, indicating Mahalath's maternal lineage.
notes.11:23: Dispersing his sons across the fortified towns secured loyalty in the provinces while preventing rival claims around the throne in Jerusalem.
notes.12:3: The Lubim were Libyans, the Cushites were peoples of Nubia and Ethiopia, and the Sukkiim were an allied North African or desert contingent serving in Egypt's army.
notes.12:5: Hebrew uses the same verb twice to underscore the measure-for-measure judgment: because Judah forsook the LORD, He in turn forsook them to Shishak.
notes.12:10: The Hebrew term translated guard literally means runners, denoting the royal footmen and palace bodyguard.
notes.13:5: A covenant of salt signifies a permanent, incorruptible, and binding pledge, reflecting salt's ancient role as a preservative in covenant meals.
notes.13:14: The Ketiv and Qere preserve two slightly different participial spellings of the Hebrew verb for blowing trumpets, with identical meaning.
notes.13:19: The Ketiv reads Ephron, whereas the Qere followed here reads Ephrain; the Hebrew word translated villages literally means its daughters, denoting dependent surrounding towns.
notes.13:22: The Hebrew term midrash denotes an investigative historical account, exposition, or commentary.
notes.13:23: Following the Masoretic versification, this verse concludes chapter thirteen; many English translations number it as chapter fourteen, verse one.
notes.14:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, 14:1 corresponds to 14:2 in many English Bibles, which number MT 13:23 as 14:1.
notes.14:4: The Hebrew term hammanim denotes small stone incense altars used in illicit cultic worship.
notes.14:8: Hebrew literally reads "a thousand thousands"; Cushite refers to the region of Cush south of Egypt, often called Ethiopia.
notes.14:10: Literally "there is nothing with You to help between many and one without strength," meaning human numbers make no difference to the LORD.
notes.15:8: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "the prophecy, Oded the prophet," naming the father of Azariah who spoke in 15:1.
notes.15:16: Hebrew em ("mother") is used broadly here for Asa's grandmother Maachah, who still held the royal office of queen mother (gebirah).
notes.16:1: Many interpreters reckon the thirty-fifth and thirty-sixth years (15:19; 16:1) from the division of the kingdom, since Baasha's reign ended earlier in Asa's rule (compare 1 Kings 16:8).
notes.16:2: Aram is the Hebrew name for Syria, and Chronicles uses the form Darmeseq for Damascus.
notes.16:8: The Lubim were a North African people associated with ancient Libya who fought alongside the Cushites.
notes.16:10: Hebrew beth hammahpekheth literally means "house of the stocks," a prison where captives were confined in a twisting wooden restraint.
notes.16:14: This great burning was a royal ceremonial fire of fragrant spices made in the king's honor, distinct from his burial in the hewn tomb.
notes.17:6: Literally "his heart was lifted up," an expression that elsewhere denotes pride, here used positively of courageous devotion in the ways of the LORD.
notes.17:8: Follows the Qere reading "Shemiramoth"; the Ketiv spelling is "Shemarimoth."
notes.17:13: Hebrew "melakhah" literally means "work" or "enterprise," here referring to abundant supplies and royal works stored in the cities of Judah.
notes.18:8: Follows the Qere reading "Micaiah" (Mikayehu); the Ketiv has the shortened spelling "Mikahu."
notes.18:14: In the Hebrew text, Ahab addresses the prophet here using the shortened form "Micah."
notes.18:20: Hebrew uses the definite article, literally "the spirit," a common Hebrew narrative usage for introducing a specific figure in a vision.
notes.18:33: Follows the Qere singular reading "your hand"; the Ketiv reads the plural "your hands."
notes.19:7: Hebrew "partiality" is literally "lifting up of faces," an idiom for showing unjust favoritism in judgment.
notes.19:8: Follows the Masoretic text "and they returned to Jerusalem"; some ancient versions reflect a different vocalization meaning "for the inhabitants of Jerusalem."
notes.19:10: "Between bloodshed and bloodshed" refers to judging different kinds of homicide, such as distinguishing accidental manslaughter from deliberate murder.
notes.20:1: The Masoretic Text reads "some of the Ammonites," whereas the Septuagint reads "some of the Meunites" (compare 2 Chronicles 26:7).
notes.20:2: The Masoretic Text reads "from Aram" (Syria); one Hebrew manuscript and many commentators suggest "from Edom," given the southern location of En Gedi.
notes.20:25: The Masoretic Text reads "corpses" (pegarim), while a few Hebrew manuscripts read "garments" (begadim), differing by a single consonant.
notes.20:26: The Hebrew name Berachah means "blessing," echoing the people's blessing of the LORD there.
notes.21:2: The Masoretic Text calls Jehoshaphat "king of Israel," reflecting the Chronicler's broader covenantal use of "Israel" for Judah, and lists two sons with variants of the name Azariah (Azaryah and Azaryahu).
notes.21:17: Jehoahaz is an alternate form of the name Ahaziah (22:1), reversing the position of the divine name element.
